correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥2 and γ>0, renewal convolution yields exactly the normalized centered event-train spectrum. Subtracting one gives 2(Re(1+iz)^n−1)/|(1+iz)^n−1|². With z=tanθ, strict derivative sign and alternating extrema prove exactly floor(n/2)−1 simple positive roots; endpoint zero/high-frequency limits, n=1 Poisson case and interval indexing were checked analytically. A generator-resolvent numerical comparison and exact finite-degree symbolic root counts passed 4464 assertions, corroborating but not replacing the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The exact event-spectrum formula and homogeneous directed-ring waiting law are established in Brandes (arXiv:0802.2233v1) and general renewal theory. What remains after subtracting prior implications is a complete integer-stage classification of how often the counted-return-jump spectrum intersects the Poisson shot-noise plateau, with strict simplicity, alternation, and localization. Detailed relevant portions of the closest full preprint were inspected, and no such all-finite-stage theorem was found. Indexed historical summaries and alternative formulations were checked, but strong priority risk from uninspected broader renewal-phase literature remains.
residual_risks: The general homogeneous-ring noise formula in Brandes may lead to the classification in older uninspected secondary literature even though the count was not stated in examined full text.
Alternative exact spectral-band or trigonometric root-count classification may exist under Erlang, renewal, gamma, or shot-noise terminology.
The 2025 state-observable spectral-peak paper was accessible only in abstract, so no whole-document noncoverage is asserted.

value.rationale: A hidden-stage transport cycle has a physically natural counted-return-jump noise spectrum with a measurable Poisson reference plateau. The exact number of crossing bands is a scale-free signature of stage count, gives a universal strict alternating sign pattern, and is fully classified for all n and γ. It establishes a nontrivial global root-count invariant from the known renewal spectrum rather than an arbitrary small-parameter example or a mere restatement of the transform.
